name: Hari chai
traditionalUses: A lighter alternative to milk tea
kitchenUse: A teaspoon of leaves or one bag steeped in water just off the boil for two to three minutes.

typicalUse.adultAmount: Up to 3–4 cups of brewed tea a day
typicalUse.note: Not a classical Ayurvedic herb, so no classical properties are recorded. Brewed tea is very different from concentrated extract capsules.

cautions.note: Concentrated green tea extract (capsules and weight-loss products) has caused liver injury, sometimes severe. Brewed tea has not been linked to this.

refs.locator: What Do We Know About Safety?

cautions.note: Contains caffeine; keep total caffeine within what your doctor advises in pregnancy and while breastfeeding.

refs.locator: What Do We Know About Safety?

cautions.note: Caffeine can raise heart rate and blood pressure in sensitive people.

interactions.effect: Large amounts can reduce the effect of the beta-blocker nadolol.

refs.locator: What Do We Know About Safety?

interactions.effect: Green tea extract can lower blood levels of atorvastatin.

refs.locator: What Do We Know About Safety?

evidence.summary: Many studies, but results for weight, heart health and other uses are inconsistent.
